question: Despite a large number of return decisions being issued in the European Union, a significant proportion of third-country nationals with no legal right to stay have still not returned to their countries of origin. The new European framework on returns provides, among other things, for the possibility of setting up return hubs in safe third countries. In view of the above, can the Commission answer the following: 1.

What specific and measurable target is it setting to increase the rate of actual enforcement of return decisions obliging third-country nationals to leave the territory of the EU and within what timeframe does it expect this target to be achieved?
When does it consider that the first common European return hubs can begin operating in safe third countries and what initiatives is it taking to conclude the necessary agreements?
Which third countries have already been approached or are being considered by the Commission or Member States for the establishment of such centres and what criteria will be used for their selection?
answer: EN on behalf of the European Commission (29.10.2026) The Return Regulation1 gives Member States the necessary tools to make returns more efficient, with swifter, simpler and more effective procedures across the EU, in full respect of fundamental rights. It is for the Member States to carry out return procedures and enforce returns, and to take the necessary measures, including targets if necessary, for doing so.

The Return Regulation, once in force, will allow Member States to return illegally staying third-country nationals subject to an order to leave to a return hub, namely to a third country with which there is an agreement or arrangement on the basis of which the third-country national is accepted. For this, the conditions set out in Article 14 of the Return Regulation need to be fulfilled.

The Commission, in cooperation with Member States, works with third countries to improve the effectiveness of return and enhance third countries’ cooperation on readmission. The Commission is not negotiating agreements or arrangements with third countries to establish a return hub.
1 Proposal for a Regulation of the European Parliament and of the Council establishing a common system for the

return of third-country nationals staying illegally in the Union, and repealing Directive 2008/115/EC of the European Parliament and the Council, Council Directive 2001/40/EC and Council Decision 2004/191/EC. https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/?uri=CELEX%3A52025PC0101.
